definition: A small cylinder that thread, wire, or film is wound around.

collocations.example: She unwound a spool of thread to sew the torn hem.
The machine winds the fine wire onto a spool automatically.

definition: To wear or display something proudly, so that people notice it.

collocations.example: He arrived at the office sporting a new haircut.
The team proudly sported their new uniforms at the game.

definition: Very dirty, unpleasant conditions, especially caused by poverty or neglect.

collocations.example: After losing his job, he was living in squalor.
The refugees were forced to endure abject squalor in the camp.

definition: A thin sheet with a design cut out, used to paint the design onto a surface.

collocations.example: She carefully cut a stencil from a sheet of thin cardboard.
The artist painted the letters through a stencil onto the wall.

definition: A small tube that doctors place inside a blood vessel to keep it open.

collocations.example: The surgeon placed a stent to keep the artery open.
Doctors inserted a coronary stent to restore blood flow to his heart.

definition: To unfairly treat someone or something as shameful or bad.

collocations.example: Society should not stigmatize sufferers of mental illness.
Many patients feel stigmatized when they admit they need help.

definition: A fixed amount of money paid regularly, often to a student or trainee.

collocations.example: The internship offers a small monthly stipend to cover living costs.
Graduate students receive a stipend while they teach and do research.

definition: The layer of the Earth's atmosphere that lies above the layer where weather happens.

collocations.example: Weather balloons can rise into the upper stratosphere before they burst.
The rocket climbed quickly until it reached the stratosphere.

definition: A long, narrow strip of colored paper or ribbon used as a decoration.

collocations.example: They hung colorful streamers across the hall for the party.
The children threw paper streamers into the air at midnight.

definition: Willing to obey others and accept their control without resisting.

collocations.example: The dog lowered its head into a submissive posture.
He was quiet and submissive to authority all his life.

definition: (Of food, especially fruit or meat) full of juice and tasting very good.

collocations.example: The restaurant served a thick, succulent steak with roasted vegetables.
If you cook it slowly, the chicken will remain succulent.

definition: To feed a baby or young animal with milk from the breast or udder.

collocations.example: Mother seals come ashore to suckle their young on the beach.
A hungry infant will instinctively suckle at the breast.

definition: The force that makes things stick together or pulls liquid or air by removing air.

collocations.example: The pump creates suction to draw water up the pipe.
The hook has a suction cup that sticks to the tile.

definition: The state of having enough of something.

collocations.example: The region now enjoys a sufficiency of clean drinking water.
The program aims to help families reach economic sufficiency.

definition: To slowly spread through or over something, especially with light, color, or feeling.

collocations.example: The setting sun began to suffuse the sky with pink light.
Her face was suffused with a warm glow of happiness.

definition: (Of weather) uncomfortably hot and humid.

collocations.example: We sat outside on a sultry summer evening, fanning ourselves.
By midday the air had grown sultry and heavy.

definition: Various; of several different kinds.

collocations.example: She packed pens, tape, and other sundry items into the box.
The sale was open to all and sundry.

definition: An extremely powerful computer that can process huge amounts of data very quickly.

collocations.example: The university plans to build a supercomputer for climate research.
The simulation runs on a supercomputer at the national laboratory.

definition: Something that you believe is true without having proof.

collocations.example: His whole argument is based on supposition, not real evidence.
The plan rested on a false supposition about customer demand.

definition: Food and drink that people and animals need to stay alive and healthy.

collocations.example: The small garden provided enough sustenance for the whole family.
For these villagers, the river is their main source of sustenance.

definition: A small piece of soft material used to clean a wound or take a sample from the body.

collocations.example: The nurse cleaned the cut with a cotton swab and antiseptic.
The doctor took a swab from the patient's throat for testing.

definition: A large amount of a drink swallowed quickly in one gulp.

collocations.example: He took a swig of cold water after the long run.
She paused, then drank a long swig straight from the bottle.

definition: To cheat someone in order to take their money.

collocations.example: He was jailed for trying to swindle elderly investors.
She schemed to swindle her uncle out of his savings.

definition: To feel so much excitement, delight, or admiration that you can hardly control yourself.

collocations.example: Teenage fans swoon over the handsome young actor.
His beautiful singing voice made the whole audience swoon.

definition: A large tree with broad leaves and smooth bark, common in North America.

collocations.example: A huge sycamore tree shaded the whole front yard.
Birds nested in the branches of a towering sycamore.

definition: The small gap where one nerve cell passes signals to another.

collocations.example: Chemical messengers carry the signal as it crosses the synapse.
At a chemical synapse, neurons communicate using tiny molecules.

definition: The extra benefit produced when people or things work together, greater than their separate effects.

collocations.example: Combining their skills created synergy across the whole department.
There is clear synergy between the design and marketing teams.

definition: To arrange facts or numbers in columns or a table.

collocations.example: The researchers tabulated the results in a clear, simple table.
She neatly tabulated the survey responses by age group.

definition: Cheap, showy, and in poor taste.

collocations.example: The hotel lobby was full of tacky plastic decorations.
The bright neon sign made the shop look tacky.

definition: A very small amount; a little (used in the phrase 'a tad').

collocations.example: This shirt is a tad too tight across the shoulders.
Add just a tad of salt to balance the sweetness.

definition: The young form of a frog or toad, which lives in water and has a tail.

collocations.example: The children love to catch tadpoles in the shallow pond.

collocations.collocation: a tadpole grows into a frog
collocations.example: Within weeks, a tadpole grows into a small frog.

definition: A sharp, curved claw of a bird that hunts, such as an eagle or hawk.

collocations.example: The eagle seized the fish with its sharp talons.
The owl gripped the branch tightly with its talons.

definition: A lively ballroom dance from Argentina, performed by two people together.

collocations.example: They learned to dance the tango on their honeymoon.
The café filled with the sound of romantic tango music.

definition: Equal in effect to something, usually something bad.

collocations.example: Criticizing the king was once tantamount to treason.
Resigning now would be tantamount to admitting he was guilty.

definition: A pattern of crossing colored stripes, traditionally Scottish, or cloth with this pattern.

collocations.example: Her scarf had a bright red and green tartan pattern.
Many Scots proudly wear tartan on special occasions.

definition: Having a warm orange-brown color.

collocations.example: The lion's tawny fur blended with the dry grass.
The autumn leaves had turned tawny in color.

definition: A hard, yellowish-brown wood from a tropical tree, often used for furniture.

collocations.example: The dining table is made from solid teak.
The garden bench was beautifully made of teak.

definition: A small, formal detail in a rule or law that can affect a decision.

collocations.example: The case was dismissed on a legal technicality.
He avoided the fine on a technicality.

definition: An expert in science, technology, or management who holds power in government or business.

collocations.example: The new minister is a respected technocrat with years of experience.
For a while the country was ruled by unelected technocrats.

definition: The practice of not drinking alcohol.

collocations.example: The temperance movement campaigned against the sale of alcohol.
He practiced temperance and never touched alcohol again.

definition: A violent storm with very strong winds.

collocations.example: The small boat was tossed about by a raging tempest.
The sailors were caught in a tempest far from shore.

definition: The quality of being very determined and not giving up.

collocations.example: She succeeded through sheer tenacity and hard work.
The team defended their narrow lead with great tenacity.

definition: A thin, curling part of a climbing plant that wraps around objects for support.

collocations.example: The vine sent out curling tendrils along the wooden fence.
A thin tendril wraps around the stake for support.

definition: A hard, reddish-brown clay used to make pots, tiles, and statues.

collocations.example: Herbs grew in a row of small terracotta pots.
The roof tiles were traditionally made of terracotta.

definition: A hormone that controls the development of male sexual features.

collocations.example: Regular exercise can help raise a man's testosterone levels.
Some men take supplements that claim to boost testosterone.

definition: Relating to the connection between heat and other forms of energy.

collocations.example: The system slowly reaches thermodynamic equilibrium with its surroundings.
Every engine must obey the basic thermodynamic laws.

definition: A horse of a pure breed, especially one bred for racing.

collocations.example: They paid a fortune for a champion thoroughbred racehorse.
The farm has bred thoroughbreds for over fifty years.

definition: A main road or public route that people travel along.

collocations.example: The shop sits on a busy thoroughfare in the city center.
Street vendors set up their stalls along the thoroughfare.

definition: A period of violent struggle or intense difficulty.

collocations.example: The old empire was clearly in its death throes.
The country is in the throes of a deep recession.

definition: A songbird with a brown back and a spotted breast, known for its beautiful song.

collocations.example: A song thrush sang loudly from the top of the hedge.
A thrush built its nest in the old apple tree.

definition: To prepare and cultivate land for growing crops.

collocations.example: Farmers till the soil each spring before planting seeds.
The freshly tilled field was ready for the new crop.

definition: To make light, high ringing sounds, like a small bell.

collocations.example: The sleigh bells tinkle as the horse trots along.
Glass chimes tinkle in the breeze outside the window.

definition: A large, heavy, and usually serious book.

collocations.example: He pulled a weighty tome from the dusty library shelf.
She wrote a massive tome of ancient history.

definition: A method of making images of the inside of the body in thin slices.

collocations.example: The hospital used computed tomography to examine the injury.
The doctor ordered a tomography scan of the patient's chest.

definition: A clear precious stone, often yellow or blue, used in jewelry.

collocations.example: She wore a ring set with a sparkling blue topaz.
He gave his wife a topaz ring for their anniversary.

definition: To move or walk in an unsteady way, as if about to fall.

collocations.example: The injured player slowly tottered to his feet.
The toddler took two steps, then tottered and fell.

definition: Easily upset, offended, or annoyed.

collocations.example: She is very touchy about her exam results.
He has been a bit touchy since losing his job.

definition: To make someone's hair or something untidy by rubbing or pulling it.

collocations.example: She reached down to tousle the little boy's hair.
The wind gave her a charmingly tousled look.

definition: A device that changes one form of energy or signal into another.

collocations.example: A pressure transducer measures the force inside the pipe.
In the sensor, the transducer converts sound into electrical signals.

definition: Lying or placed across something, from one side to the other.

collocations.example: A transverse beam supports the roof across the whole room.
The crack ran transverse to the main axis of the bone.

definition: To shock and upset someone so severely that it causes lasting emotional harm.

collocations.example: Witnessing such violence can deeply traumatize a child.
The survivors were deeply traumatized by the earthquake.

definition: A frame of crossing strips of wood or metal that supports climbing plants.

collocations.example: Roses climbed up the wooden garden trellis by the gate.
The ivy will climb a trellis if you train it.

definition: A feeling of fear or worry about something that is going to happen.

collocations.example: He approached the job interview with trepidation.
The soldiers waited for the order with fear and trepidation.

definition: To sing or sound with a high, quavering, rapidly repeated note.

collocations.example: At dawn the birds trill from every tree in the garden.
The singer can trill a high note with ease.

definition: Having three parts, or involving three groups or countries.

collocations.example: The three nations signed a tripartite agreement on trade.
The report is tripartite in structure, with three clear sections.

definition: One of three children born to the same mother at the same time.

collocations.example: The couple were amazed to learn they would have identical triplets.
She gave birth to triplets after a long pregnancy.

definition: Small details or facts that are not important.

collocations.example: They chatted about everyday trivia over their morning coffee.
The meeting got bogged down in trivia and achieved nothing.

definition: A round fungus that grows underground and is highly valued as a gourmet food.

collocations.example: The chef shaved a black truffle over the fresh pasta.
Trained pigs are used to hunt for truffles in the forest.

definition: To make something shorter by cutting off the top or the end.

collocations.example: The system will truncate the text if it is too long.
They released a truncated version of the original report.

definition: To move slowly and heavily, especially on wheels.

collocations.example: The old bus trundled along the bumpy country road.
The worker trundled a heavy cart across the yard.

definition: A short, thick, rounded underground stem, such as a potato, from which new plants grow.

collocations.example: Each potato tuber can grow into a whole new plant.
Gardeners plant the tubers in early spring.

definition: A long piece of cloth wound around the head, worn in some cultures.

collocations.example: Many Sikh men wear a turban every day.
The old man wore a neatly tied white turban.

definition: A large bird raised for its meat, especially eaten on holidays.

collocations.example: The family gathered around a golden roast turkey for dinner.
The farm raises turkeys for the holiday season.

definition: A very long, pointed tooth that sticks out from the mouth of some animals.

collocations.example: Hunters prized the elephant for its valuable ivory tusks.
The small statue was carved from a walrus tusk.

definition: A man's formal black jacket or suit worn on special evening occasions.

collocations.example: The groom decided to wear a tuxedo for the wedding.
He showed up at the dance in a rented tuxedo.

definition: A small, thin branch of a tree or bush.

collocations.example: A dry twig snapped under his boot in the quiet forest.
Try not to snap a twig and scare the deer away.

definition: A sudden, short, sharp pain.

collocations.example: She felt a twinge as she bent down to tie her shoe.
There was a sharp twinge in his lower back.

definition: The style, size, and arrangement of printed letters and text.

collocations.example: The poster used bold typography to grab attention.
She studied the art of typography at design school.

definition: A system for sorting things into groups according to their types.

collocations.example: Linguistic typology compares the structures of different languages.
The study proposed a typology of leadership styles.

definition: Seeming to be present everywhere at the same time; extremely common.

collocations.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern daily life.
The ubiquitous smartphone has changed how we communicate.

definition: Relating to the cord that connects an unborn baby to its mother.

collocations.example: The nurse gently clamped the baby's umbilical cord.
The doctor let the father cut the umbilical cord.

definition: A situation in which everyone agrees completely about something.

collocations.example: The committee struggled to reach unanimity on the budget.
The vote showed complete unanimity among the members.

definition: To do less well than you are able to, or than expected.

collocations.example: Some bright children underachieve at school because they are bored.
Students without support often tend to underachieve.

definition: A feeling or tendency that is hidden but can still be sensed.

collocations.example: There was an undercurrent of tension throughout the meeting.
A strong undercurrent of resentment ran through the team.

definition: A person or team that is expected to lose a contest or struggle.

collocations.example: Crowds love to root for the underdog in a close match.
The film tells a classic underdog story about a young boxer.

definition: To provide too little money for something.

collocations.example: The plan would underfund schools in poorer areas.
The hospital has been chronically underfunded for years.

definition: To think that someone or something is less good or important than they really are.

collocations.example: Beginners often underrate the difficulty of learning a language.
He is a badly underrated actor who deserves more praise.

definition: To unroll or spread out something that was folded or rolled up.

collocations.example: At dawn the soldiers unfurled a flag over the fort.
The sails unfurl as the crew pulls the ropes.

definition: An imaginary animal like a white horse with a single horn on its forehead.

collocations.example: The tapestry showed a mythical unicorn in a green forest.
In the story, the princess learns to ride a unicorn.

definition: Difficult to move, carry, or manage because of its size, weight, or complexity.

collocations.example: The old sofa was an unwieldy object to carry upstairs.
The old system became too unwieldy to use efficiently.

definition: The process or cost of keeping something in good condition.

collocations.example: The family could no longer afford the upkeep of the estate.
The garden needs regular upkeep to stay beautiful.

definition: The final result of a situation.

collocations.example: The upshot of the meeting was a new company policy.
The upshot is that we must cut our spending.

definition: To take people's attention away from someone, making yourself seem more important.

collocations.example: He loves to upstage a rival whenever he gets the chance.
The host was upstaged by a surprise celebrity guest.

definition: A person who has recently gained wealth or power and behaves arrogantly.

collocations.example: The veteran manager resented the young upstart in the office.
His rivals dismissed him as an upstart with no real experience.
